notes: Protection warrior at 60 in Defensive Stance with a shield: Shield Slam and Revenge on cooldown, Shield Block whenever its buff is down, Battle Shout kept up, Thunder Clap held on the boss, Sunder Armor as the global-cooldown filler and Heroic Strike with spare rage. Every priority was measured on the engine's tank harness (a level 63 boss, one 2 second melee swing, steady healing; sim/warrior/tank_warrior's TestRotationVariations records the figures): Shield Block cuts damage taken by about 18 percent, a Thunder Clap upkeep by another 16 percent for 6 percent of threat, Sunder Armor as the filler adds about 24 percent threat, and the Heroic Strike threshold moves nothing because a Forever tank is cooldown-limited, not rage-limited, at this gear. Last Stand and Shield Wall are gated on health: they never fire on a fight the healers hold and cut the chance of death on one they do not. Demoralizing Shout is kept up after Thunder Clap (round 14, owner ruling: the tank boss carries a Classic creature's attack power, 268 at level 63, and a creature's swing scales with it as a share, so the shout's 204 takes about 23 percent off every swing): raid 60, 10,000 iterations, damage taken about 22 percent lower for about 2 percent less threat. Every rank named here is checked against the spellconst of the newest client build. 2026-11-02 (launch guide rewrite, round-11 engine, 10000 iterations, seeds 1 and 50001, raid / bare): Bloodrage before the pull and Battle Shout with its rage, as a tank plays it (the shout at -1 s alone had no rage to cast with), so the first Sunder or Shield Slam is paid for: threat 1082 to 1080 a second (-0.2%, about two standard errors) and damage taken unchanged over the full fight, threat unchanged over the first 20 seconds; kept because it is how the pull is played. Swapping Revenge and Shield Slam, and Shield Block after Shield Slam, were inside the error too. 2026-11-03 (round 12): the pre-pull Battle Shout is skipped when a raid warrior's shout is already up; solo and bare levels still shout. 2026-11-12 (sim-accuracy, Protection warrior lane): Bloodrage pays its fifth of base health and Thunder Clap carries its attack power share, both from the client and the Forever logs; no priority moved, the Heroic Strike gate at 40 re-checked against 30, 50 and 60.

expected_idle.reason: Shield Block needs a shield and the ladder's character carries none (its off hand is a weapon slot only for dual-wielding classes), so the engine refuses the cast at every level. A tank in the tank fight, shield on, casts it about 34 times in 180 seconds.

Shield Slam needs a shield for the same reason (its cast condition is a shield in the off hand), so the shieldless ladder character never casts it. In the tank fight it lands on every cooldown, about 30 times in 180 seconds.
Defensive Stance is a stance-dance guard, not part of the cycle: the engine starts a tank warrior in it (sim/warrior/tank_warrior's tankStance) so the cast condition, not being in it, is never true.

Shield Wall is gated on health below 40 percent and on a shield; the ladder fight does not hurt the character, so it correctly never fires. The tank harness shows it cutting the chance of death on a boss the healers cannot hold.

sources.label: Talents Forever Deep Dive stream: Shield Block 2 charges and 7 s, Thunder Clap usable in Defensive Stance, Shield Wall 15 min / 60 percent for 12 s (single-source)

priorityList.notes: Live in it: the threat bonus, Revenge, Shield Block and Shield Wall all need it.
Below 35% health: 30% of your maximum health for 20 seconds, lost again when it ends.
Below 40% health: 60% less damage taken for 12 seconds, on a 15-minute cooldown.

Once before the pull, then whenever rage is under 60: 10 rage at once and 10 more over 10 seconds, a quarter more with your first point of Improved Bloodrage at 10 and half again from 11. It costs a fifth of your base health, so it will not fire when you are nearly dead.
Whenever it is down: 75% more block chance for 7 seconds, off the global cooldown. Every block also lights Revenge.
The moment it lights: a dodge, parry or block opens it, and it is the most threat per rage you have.
On cooldown: a hard hit with a very high amount of threat, and it grows with your block value.
Keep it on the boss: its attack speed slow is a straight cut to the damage you take, and its damage grows with your attack power. Refresh it in its last 3 seconds.
Keep it on the boss: the attack power it strips takes a real slice off every swing. One is enough, since it does not stack with a druid's Demoralizing Roar. Refresh it in its last 3 seconds.
Whenever it drops. In a raid at 60 another warrior's Battle Shout is the same aura, so you only shout when nobody else has.
On every free global: five stacks for the raid, then flat threat on every cast.
Only above 40 rage, queued on your next swing. It costs no global cooldown, so it never delays the buttons above.
